videos.title: The ENTIRE History of Rome in 26 Minutes
videos.description:
Rome was never the strongest power of the ancient world. It lost battles, armies and whole fleets. But it had one habit almost no one else had: it turned its enemies into Romans. This history documentary covers the entire history of Rome, from Romulus and Remus and the Roman Republic to Hannibal, Julius Caesar, Augustus and the Roman Empire, Nero, the Colosseum, Constantine, the fall of Rome in 476, Byzantium and the fall of Constantinople in 1453.

videos.title: The ENTIRE History of Russia in 28 Minutes
videos.description: Russia sits on one huge open plain with no mountains or sea to hide behind. For a thousand years its answer has been the same: push the border further out. It became the largest country on Earth, and it has never felt safe. This history documentary covers the entire history of Russia, from the Vikings and Kievan Rus to the Mongols, Ivan the Terrible, Peter the Great, Catherine the Great, Napoleon in 1812, the Revolution, Stalin, Stalingrad, Gagarin, the fall of the Soviet Union and Russia today.

videos.title: The ENTIRE History of Egypt: The River That Outlived Empires
videos.description:
Persians, Greeks, Romans, Arabs, Turks, the French and the British all ruled Egypt. Every one of those empires is gone. Egypt is still here, because the river kept flowing. This history documentary covers the entire history of Egypt, from the green Sahara and the first pharaohs to the pyramids, Tutankhamun, Cleopatra, Saladin, the Mamluks, Napoleon, the Suez Canal, Nasser and Egypt today.

videos.title: The ENTIRE History of Japan in 29 Minutes
videos.description:
Japan borrowed writing and Buddhism from China, then made them its own. It took guns from Portugal, then gave them up. It shut itself away from the world for more than two hundred years, then became a modern power in a single generation. This history documentary covers the entire history of Japan, from the Jomon and Queen Himiko to the samurai, the shoguns, the Meiji Restoration, World War II, the economic miracle and Japan today.

videos.title: The ENTIRE History of China in 28 Minutes
videos.description:
China fell apart into warring kingdoms, was split between rival dynasties, conquered by Mongols and Manchus, carved up by foreign powers and torn by civil war. And every time, it pulled itself back together. This history documentary covers the entire history of China, from the Yellow River, the Shang oracle bones and the First Emperor to the Ming, the Opium Wars, the People's Republic and China today.

videos.title: The ENTIRE History of Iran in 28 Minutes
videos.description:
Alexander burned its capital. The Arabs ended its empire. The Turks took its throne and the Mongols destroyed its cities. And every time, a few generations later, the conquerors were speaking Persian. This history documentary covers the entire history of Iran, from Elam and the Persian Empire of Cyrus the Great to the Islamic Revolution, the war of 2026 and Iran today.

videos.title: The ENTIRE History of Korea in 28 Minutes
videos.description:
When whales fight, the shrimp's back breaks. For two thousand years Korea has been the shrimp between China, the Mongols, Japan, Russia and America, and every empire that tried to swallow it is gone. This history documentary covers the entire history of Korea, from the Dangun legend and the dolmen builders to the Korean War, the Miracle on the Han River and Korea today.

videos.title: He Walked Around the World for 28 Years. He Just Got Home
videos.description:
On November 1st, 1998, a former British Army paratrooper from Hull set off from Punta Arenas, at the bottom of Chile, with a tent, a few hundred dollars, a cheap camera and a handcart he later called "The Beast". His rule: walk home to England with unbroken footsteps. No car, no train, no plane, and no going home until he arrived on foot. He planned to be back in twelve years.

videos.title: He Drifted 41 Days Across the Pacific. His Cousin Didn't Make It
videos.description:
On September 16, 2026, Independence Day in Papua New Guinea, 18-year-old Luka Rahan and his 16-year-old cousin Cletus Manman went out fishing from their village in North Bougainville in a small dinghy with a 15-horsepower engine. On the way home the engine died: water had got into the petrol. They had no anchor, and the current carried them north-east into the open Pacific.
